s1.text:
How to read these boards

Each board is one block-theme template at 1440px, built from the real design-system CSS. Columns follow the site's navigation, left to right, top to bottom.

Blue chips name the pattern and blocks that build each section: core/* are WordPress core blocks, ot/* are the theme's custom blocks.

The header and footer boards are the two template parts; every page imports them.

Turn the chips off with the Show blocks tweak on any board.

s2.text:
Phone boards (390px)

A phone board sits to the right of its desktop template and imports it, so the two never drift apart: edit the 1440px board and the 390px one follows.

Below 1024px the header swaps its navigation for the overlay menu; below 832px every split stacks to one column; cards go one-up below 576px.

Block chips are off by default on phone boards; turn them on with the Show blocks tweak.

t4.text: Our team: the team page, the joint page and one profile per agent

s3.text:
Agent profiles

One single-agent.html template serves every agent: Brandon, Kaitlyn and anyone who joins later. Switch the board's Agent tweak between brandon, kaitlyn and template.

Built for search and answer engines from the start: ProfilePage + Person JSON-LD linked by @id to the team and REWAP, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, an answer-first summary, quick facts and a dated update line.

Built for conversion: message and call above the fold, a fixed phone action bar, service links and a form attributed to the agent.

Unconfirmed facts stay as [bracketed placeholders]; photos are interim crops of the team portrait.

s4.text:
Community guides

One single-community.html template serves all 27 town guides (Tiers 1 to 3), from a researched record per town (tools/data/towns). Every fact carries its source URL; the guide lists them at the foot.

Built for search and answer engines: an h1 of "Living in (town), MA", a 40 to 60 word answer as the lead, quick facts, a dated market table (The Warren Group, 2025), WebPage + City JSON-LD.

Fair housing: describe places, housing, transit and history; never who lives there; schools are a DESE link, never a rating.

Towns the source reports only by village (Barnstable) show a village table instead of a town median.

The list of towns is proposed until the team confirms it.

t5.text: Lead management: the built-in CRM (ot-leads plugin, admin screens)

s5.text:
Lead management (ot-leads)

These are WordPress admin screens, not theme templates. They live in the ot-leads plugin so leads survive any theme change (docs/wordpress-architecture.md).

Every site form saves here. Routing assigns the lead; the team works it in the inbox and pipeline; an outside CRM (webhook or Follow Up Boss) is optional and the site always keeps its own record.

AI drafts nurture emails only from the lead's record and the site's sourced content, runs fair-housing and number checks, and waits for a person to approve.

All leads shown are demo data. Spec: docs/leads-crm-nurture-spec.md.

s6.text:
IDX: still to decide (docs/idx-options.md)

Listings come from MLS PIN through a licensed IDX product; the theme only styles them.

Recommended launch: Showcase IDX Essentials ($94.95/mo, 2 seats; listings on our domain and indexable), or IDX Broker Core ($87/mo) if its listing pages prove crawlable. Interim: MLS PIN's free IDX Links.

Later, only if a licensable product is the goal: Realtyna MLS On The Fly ($449/mo for MLS PIN) or a direct MLS PIN feed ($100 brokerage / $525 vendor, approval required).

Not at launch: RealScout (duplicates ot-leads nurture) and all-in-one platforms (replace the site).

Vendor lead events (registrations, saved searches, showings) flow into ot-leads. Published prices, not quotes; confirm in writing.
